chapter_title: The Chapter of the Nazorean who questions the Teac
spiritual_reading:
The discernment that proceeds from what is Divine is not itself evil, but is the operation of order opposing evil, restraining it and setting bounds to it. Yet in the outward appearance that operation is described as going forth to punish and to destroy, because it removes and brings to an end what is contrary, so that the evil may be annulled and its power to act may be impeded within the person. In doing so it turns the evil back upon its own origin within the perverted will and understanding, and makes it manifest as belonging to the evildoer.

Still, the Divine does nothing of evil to them; they do it to themselves. Their own acts, because they are from their own evil love and confirming falsity, are what judge them, and by their own choice they are carried into the vehement craving and torment of evil love.
assessment: Only a trivial mid-word lacuna occurs in this excerpt (ev[il to] them), and the surviving context fixes it unambiguously. No deeper correspondential reconstruction was required.
